question: What are ways to cool the center-of-mass (CoM) motion of levitated nanoparticles?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer identifies measurement-based feedback cooling as the (most common) way to cool the CoM motion of levitated nanoparticles.
examples: Feedback cooling is currently the most commonly used method
Measurement-based feedback control can cool the CoM motion

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer describes the mechanism: measure real-time position, derive instantaneous velocity, and apply an opposing force, e.g., via scattering forces from laser beams.
examples: Calculate the instantaneous velocity from the position signal and apply a force opposing the velocity
Feedback cooling by scattering forces from three orthogonal 532 nm laser beams

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer describes levitating a femtogram dielectric particle in cryogenic free space, where thermal decoherence is suppressed and measurement backaction dominates, enabling quantum control and CoM cooling via measurement-based feedback.
examples: Levitating a femtogram dielectric particle in cryogenic free space suppresses thermal effects
With an efficient quantum measurement, we exert quantum control and cool the CoM motion by measurement-based feedback

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer quantifies cooling performance, e.g., millikelvin mode temperatures (1.5 mK at 5.2 mPa, from 297 K) or near-ground-state occupancies (about 0.65 motional quanta, state purity 0.43).
examples: Cooling from room temperature to 1.5 mK at low pressure
An average occupancy of 0.65 motional quanta, corresponding to a state purity of 0.43

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: The answer explains that lowering gas pressure reduces the gas-collision heating rate while the feedback cooling rate stays roughly constant, so the final temperature drops (proportional to pressure at constant gain).
examples: Reducing the pressure reduces the heating rate from air-molecule collisions while the cooling rate remains constant
At constant feedback gain, the mode temperature is proportional to pressure

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer gives hardware and implementation details: orthogonal 532 nm cooling beams (~1% of trapping-beam intensity), AOM-controlled power modulated proportionally to instantaneous velocity (plus an offset to shift the trap centre), or detector calibration via thermal spectra.
examples: Three orthogonal 532 nm laser beams with intensities about 1% of the trapping beams, power controlled by acousto-optic modulators
Each beam is modulated with a signal proportional to the instantaneous velocity plus an offset

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer motivates CoM cooling: probing quantum mechanics with macroscopic objects, matter-wave/free-fall experiments, and fully controllable trapping potentials.
examples: Cooled levitated particles allow tests of quantum mechanics on a macroscopic scale
The fully controllable trapping potential makes levitated nanoparticles promising for matter-wave experiments

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer notes that free-space levitated cooling avoids an optical resonator and its bandwidth limitations, and contrasts it with tethered micromechanical oscillators cooled by radiation-pressure coupling or cavity-enhanced feedback.
examples: The absence of an optical resonator and its bandwidth limitations is advantageous
Cavity-enhanced detection schemes have been used to cool tethered oscillators to their quantum ground states

ingredients.name: valuable_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer discusses decoherence: gas collisions as a heating source at finite pressure, and thermal effects suppressed in cryogenic environments so measurement backaction dominates.
examples: Heating arises from collisions with air molecules at finite pressure
Cryogenic free space suppresses thermal effects so measurement backaction dominates decoherence
